public_rationale: Shumer's post describes METR as tracking 'real-world tasks' that a model can 'complete successfully end-to-end without human help'. It cites a figure of nearly five hours for Claude Opus 4.5. It never mentions that this figure is the 50% success horizon, and it never says the tasks are software tasks. METR's own page defines the headline horizon as the length at which an agent succeeds half the time. It also says the tasks are primarily software engineering, ML and cybersecurity, and do not cover all intellectual tasks. Both omissions Marcus names are present. His phrase 'only about coding' slightly overstates how narrow the benchmark is, but this does not change the finding that Shumer left these points out.
limitations: The live post was read in October 2026. Edits made since February cannot be fully excluded.
METR's tasks include ML and cybersecurity work, so 'only coding' is a slight simplification.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Shumer's post states that the METR figures reflect a 50% success rate, or that the tasks are software or coding tasks.
